title: Unique pure-generator-normalized evaluation of total tensor complexes
statement: Let $C$ be a category with object and morphism universes $c,v$, $J$ a Grothendieck topology, and assume $C$ is essentially small in universe $\max(c,v,r)$. Let $B_n$ be commutative ring sheaves in this coefficient universe, with maps $\tau_n:B_{n+1}\to B_n$. Use the actual semilinear systems, evaluation functor $e_n$, and sectionwise and total tensor constructions of [def-coef-semilinear-system-models], with the pure total generators of [def-coef-ringed-tensor-hom-model]. For every $n\in\mathbf N$ and arbitrary unbounded cochain complexes $P,Q$ of these systems, there is a unique isomorphism $e_n(\operatorname{Tot}(P\otimes Q))\cong\operatorname{Tot}(e_nP\otimes e_nQ)$ carrying each pure total generator represented by $x\otimes y$ in bidegree $(p,q)$, $p+q=k$, to the pure total generator of the evaluated sections $x,y$. More precisely, any specified section transport $\sigma_{M,U}:M_n(U)\to(e_nM)(U)$ heterogeneously equal to the original section gives this same generator formula. There is no K-flatness, boundedness or normalization hypothesis. The evaluation functor may be supplied as a zero-morphism-preserving functor F together with an equality F=e_n, so definitionally equal presentations of evaluation use the same assertion.

proof.text: Take the ordinary section-normalized evaluation tensor comparisons. Their naturality and the evaluation/coextension adjunction give an invertible signed total chain comparison, using preservation of the coproducts in each total degree. Invert it to obtain the evaluation-to-tensor orientation.

The coproduct inclusion equation for mapBifunctorDesc identifies the inverse total comparison on each summand. Apply it to a pure tensor and use the inverse ordinary evaluation comparison and sectionwise functoriality of evaluation. This gives the inverse comparison formula on every total pure generator.

First eliminate the specified equality F=e_n. Apply the forward comparison to the inverse generator formula and cancel the inverse comparison. Any specified section transport heterogeneously equal to the original section agrees with the canonical section transport. This proves existence with the required formula.

For uniqueness, precompose two forward comparisons with the constructed inverse. Equality of chain maps is degreewise, and maps out of the total tensor are determined on every summand by pure tensor generators. Evaluation sections are surjective, so the prescribed forward formulas and inverse generator formula give equality on every such generator. Cancel the inverse and use extensionality of isomorphisms.

theorem semilinearTotalTensorEvaluation_existsUnique (n : ℕ)
    (F : Systems.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ ⥤ SemilinearSections.Mod.{c, v, max c v r} J (B n))
    [hF0 : F.PreservesZeroMorphisms] (hF : F = SemilinearSections.evaluation J B τ n)
    (σ : ∀ (M : Systems.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ) (U : Cᵒᵖ),
      M.val.obj (op (n, U.unop)) →
        (F.obj M).val.obj U)
    (hσ : ∀ M U x, HEq (σ M U x) x)
    (P Q : CochainComplex (Systems.{c, v, max c v r} J B τ) ℤ) :
    ∃! e : (F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj
        ((totalTensor.{c, v, r} (coefficientSequenceTopology J) (systemRing J B τ)).obj (P, Q)) ≅
      (totalTensor.{c, v, r} J (B n)).obj
        ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P,
         (F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q),
      ∀ (p q k : ℤ) (h : p + q = k) (U : Cᵒᵖ)
        (x : (P.X p).val.obj (op (n, U.unop)))
        (y : (Q.X q).val.obj (op (n, U.unop))),
        (e.hom.f k).val.app U
          (σ _ U (coefficientTensorGenerator.{r, c, v} (coefficientSequenceTopology J)
            (systemRing J B τ) P Q p q k h (op (n, U.unop)) x y)) =
          coefficientTensorGenerator.{r, c, v} J (B n)
            ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj P)
            ((F.mapHomologicalComplex (.up ℤ)).obj Q)
            p q k h U (σ (P.X p) U x) (σ (Q.X q) U y)
